events.title: US October PPI release
events.why_it_matters: A hot PPI print would reinforce the December Fed hike narrative and could revive 50bp tail risk after this week's hot CPI.
events.what_to_watch: Core PPI MoM and YoY versus consensus; any upside surprise likely lifts front-end yields and the dollar.

events.title: US October retail sales
events.why_it_matters: Retail sales will show whether the US consumer is holding up under elevated rates and persistent inflation, a key input for Q4 GDP tracking.
events.what_to_watch: Control group MoM and revisions; a weak print could soften the Fed's hiking resolve, while a strong print reinforces higher-for-longer.

events.title: FOMC October meeting minutes
events.why_it_matters: The minutes will reveal how close the committee was to a larger move and the breadth of concern over sticky inflation, shaping December expectations.
events.what_to_watch: Language on 'further tightening' and any explicit discussion of a 50bp option; a hawkish read lifts December hike odds toward 100%.

events.title: December Fed hike fully priced; 50bp tail debated
events.why_it_matters: Futures now assign a 100% probability to a December hike, with debate centered on 25bp versus 50bp, driving front-end yields and rate-sensitive sectors.
events.what_to_watch: Fed speak into the blackout period and the December 9 FOMC dot plot; a 50bp move would be a regime shift for risk assets.

events.title: Nvidia Q3 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Nvidia is the bellwether for the AI capex cycle; a strong guide validates the AI trade, while any softness would hit semis and broad risk appetite.
events.what_to_watch: Data-center revenue, Q4 guidance, and commentary on Rubin ramp and supply constraints; consensus is ~$108.8B revenue and $2.47 EPS.

events.title: Anthropic IPO pricing and Nasdaq debut
events.why_it_matters: A $61B+ raise at a ~$1.2T valuation would be the largest AI listing ever, setting a valuation benchmark for private AI peers and testing public-market appetite.
events.what_to_watch: Final pricing versus the $70–78 range and first-day trading pop; a weak debut would pressure AI-linked names and late-stage venture marks.

events.title: Home Depot, Target, Walmart Q3 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Big-box retail results and holiday guidance will signal the health of the US consumer and the margin impact of tariffs and input costs.
events.what_to_watch: Comparable sales, gross margins, and holiday outlook; HD reports Nov 17, Target Nov 19, Walmart Nov 19 (pre-market).

events.title: Congress lame-duck session and Dec 11 shutdown deadline
events.why_it_matters: A government shutdown would disrupt data releases, federal spending, and market confidence just as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a short-term CR or omnibus emerges before Dec 11; Senate Democrats are pushing to attach Iran-war funding restrictions, raising friction.

events.title: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) advancing
events.why_it_matters: The tax package could include crypto tax rules and administrative changes, affecting technology and financial sectors in a thin lame-duck window.
events.what_to_watch: Senate floor action on H.R. 2347 as the vehicle; passage before Thanksgiving recess is uncertain but a surprise deal would be market-moving.

events.title: Supreme Court IEEPA tariff refunds ($166B) advance
events.why_it_matters: Importers are closer to automatic refunds of $166B in tariffs struck down under IEEPA, a major cash-flow boost for retailers and industrials.
events.what_to_watch: Implementation timeline and whether the administration attempts further legal maneuvers to slow refunds; Target and Walmart have already received partial refunds.

events.title: Section 232 robotics and industrial machinery proclamation
events.why_it_matters: Trump concluded that robotics and machinery imports threaten national security and ordered negotiations, keeping tariffs or quotas on the table for a key industrial input.
events.what_to_watch: Commerce/USTR negotiation progress and any subsequent tariff announcement; the probe covers robots, industrial machinery, and parts.

events.title: China extends suspension of 24% retaliatory tariff on US goods
events.why_it_matters: Beijing kept the 10% tariff but suspended the additional 24% for two more months, averting near-term escalation and supporting trade-exposed sectors into year-end.
events.what_to_watch: The new suspension runs through early January 2027; any signal of non-renewal would revive tariff-escalation risk.

events.title: OFAC Iran-related general licenses and sanctions actions
events.why_it_matters: New Iran-related general licenses and designations alter the sanctions perimeter for oil trade and financial flows, affecting energy risk premia.
events.what_to_watch: Scope of GLs EE and FF and whether they ease or tighten restrictions on Iranian crude exports; any tightening lifts oil.

events.title: Trump executive order on Oval Office national monument (non-market)
events.why_it_matters: A symbolic executive order with no direct market impact; included for completeness of government-actions coverage.
events.what_to_watch: Nothing market-relevant; ignore for prediction purposes.

events.title: Russia-Ukraine Abu Dhabi talks: prisoner exchange, no ceasefire
events.why_it_matters: The first face-to-face talks in nine months produced a major prisoner swap but no ceasefire or territorial progress, leaving energy-supply risk intact.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a follow-up round is scheduled and if Lavrov's refusal of an immediate ceasefire softens; any breakthrough would hit oil and European gas.

events.title: Iran denies nuclear talks; Hormuz tanker attacks keep risk premium alive
events.why_it_matters: Three tankers struck mines near Hormuz and Iran's security chief denied nuclear talks, keeping a supply-disruption premium in oil despite diplomatic rhetoric.
events.what_to_watch: Further attacks or US/Iran military escalation; EIA still sees Brent near $100 through year-end on Middle East supply constraints.

events.title: Oil falls on Iran/Ukraine peace hopes; Brent below $92
events.why_it_matters: Brent slipped below $92 as traders priced reduced geopolitical risk, but no ceasefire is in place and the risk premium can re-inflate quickly.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the down-move extends toward $88 or reverses on a fresh Hormuz incident; OPEC+ meets Nov 29.

events.title: OPEC+ maintains December output; next meeting Nov 29
events.why_it_matters: The group is holding December quotas steady while negotiating 2027 baselines; the Nov 29 meeting could set the tone for 2027 supply.
events.what_to_watch: Any hint of a quota change for 2027 or response to Hormuz disruptions; a surprise cut would lift crude.

events.title: US midterm elections: Democratic sweep of Congress
events.why_it_matters: Democrats won both chambers, ending unified Republican control and raising regulatory and fiscal-policy uncertainty into 2027.
events.what_to_watch: Lame-duck legislative priorities and early signals on Democratic oversight agendas for tech, finance, and healthcare.

events.title: US October CPI surprises hot (third straight upside)
events.why_it_matters: A third consecutive upside CPI surprise cemented a December Fed hike and revived 50bp tail risk, repricing the front end of the curve.
events.what_to_watch: Whether PPI today confirms the CPI signal; a second hot inflation print this week would harden the 50bp case.

events.title: LA-Long Beach port watchmen strike deadline (extended to Nov 20)
events.why_it_matters: A strike by ~250 terminal watchmen would disrupt terminals handling 85% of Long Beach and 33% of LA cargo, snarling holiday imports.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a deal is reached before the Nov 20 deadline; this is the fourth extension since the original Nov 1 deadline.

events.title: COP31 climate summit in Antalya
events.why_it_matters: Climate-finance and fossil-fuel transition negotiations can shape long-term policy expectations for energy and utilities.
events.what_to_watch: Any agreement on a fossil-fuel phase-out timeline or climate-finance package; outcomes are typically slow-burning rather than immediate market movers.

events.title: SEMICON Europa 2026
events.why_it_matters: The flagship European semiconductor conference spotlights advanced packaging and Europe's AI-era chip strategy, with read-through to equipment makers.
events.what_to_watch: Any announcements on EU chip incentives or advanced-packaging capacity; conference ends today.

events.title: South Korea early-November exports surge 111.9% on chips
events.why_it_matters: Semiconductors accounted for ~50% of shipments and rose 331% YoY, confirming AI-driven chip demand remains robust and supporting the global tech cycle.
events.what_to_watch: Full-month November export data (Dec 1) and chip price trends; a slowdown would challenge the AI-demand narrative ahead of Nvidia earnings.

events.title: EU CJEU AI copyright opinion
events.why_it_matters: The Advocate General's opinion distinguishes AI training inputs from infringing outputs, setting a precedent for model developers operating in Europe.
events.what_to_watch: Final CJEU judgment (timing uncertain) and whether EU AI Act implementation adopts the same distinction.

events.title: Graham Act Russia sanctions waived by executive order
events.why_it_matters: Trump implemented but waived nearly all Russia sanctions and tariffs under the Graham Act, avoiding immediate escalation but leaving the legal framework in place.
events.what_to_watch: Whether waiver authority is challenged in court or Congress attempts to force implementation.

events.title: China Q3 monetary policy report: more counter-cyclical support
events.why_it_matters: The PBoC pledged stronger counter-cyclical adjustment, higher re-lending quotas for tech and small business, and expanded PSL support, signaling further stimulus.
events.what_to_watch: October activity data (industrial production, retail sales) due mid-November; weak prints would raise expectations for additional easing.

events.title: China October industrial production and retail sales
events.why_it_matters: October activity data will show whether stimulus is stabilizing domestic demand; consensus looks for industrial production ~5.3–5.6% YoY and retail sales ~1.0% YoY.
events.what_to_watch: Retail sales weakness versus industrial production resilience; a soft consumption print would reinforce the 'external strength, internal weakness' narrative.

events.title: ECB December rate hike fully expected by economists
events.why_it_matters: All 71 economists surveyed by Reuters expect a 25bp deposit-rate hike to 2.75% in December, seen as the last of this cycle but with upside inflation risks.
events.what_to_watch: ECB communication between now and December; any hint of a pause would weaken the euro, while a hawkish tone supports EUR.

events.title: Bank of Japan December rate hike expectations build
events.why_it_matters: The BoJ's October minutes showed multiple members favor an early hike, and markets expect a move to 1.50% in December; a hike would narrow US-Japan rate differentials.
events.what_to_watch: BoJ communication and the December 18 decision; a hike supports the yen and could trigger carry-trade unwinds.

events.title: Japan Q3 GDP preliminary
events.why_it_matters: Q3 GDP is expected to slow sharply to ~0.1% QoQ from 0.4%, testing the BoJ's view that the economy can withstand further rate hikes.
events.what_to_watch: Private consumption and capex components; a contraction would complicate the December hike case.

events.title: EU informal summit in Dublin: AI and Ukraine funding
events.why_it_matters: EU leaders hold their first strategic discussion on AI and will likely revisit Ukraine funding, with a deal expected at the Nov 26-27 summit.
events.what_to_watch: Any signal on a Ukraine funding package or AI regulatory direction; concrete outcomes are more likely at the November 26-27 formal summit.

events.title: Taiwan Strait: elevated PLA activity continues
events.why_it_matters: Sustained PLA air and naval activity around Taiwan keeps tail risk for semiconductor supply chains alive, though markets have so far treated it as background noise.
events.what_to_watch: Any large-scale exercise or change in the tempo of crossings; a major escalation would hit tech and broad risk assets.

events.title: European labor strikes: Spain general strike, IG Metall warning strikes
events.why_it_matters: Spain's first general strike in 14 years and German metalworkers' warning strikes signal rising wage pressure that could feed into ECB inflation concerns.
events.what_to_watch: Whether strikes broaden or lead to higher wage settlements; a sustained wage-price spiral would harden ECB hawkishness.

events.title: Hyosung Heavy Industries union full strike (Nov 13–30)
events.why_it_matters: A full strike at Hyosung Heavy Industries' office and technical workers could disrupt power-equipment and industrial-machinery output, with read-through to Korean industrials.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the strike spreads to other Hyosung units or is resolved early; a prolonged halt would hit Korean industrial production.

events.title: FDA decisions and healthcare conferences in window
events.why_it_matters: Savara's FDA decision (Nov 22) and residual read-through from AASLD and AHA conferences could move small-cap biotech, but no mega-cap binary event is scheduled.
events.what_to_watch: Savara's molgramostim PDUFA date on Nov 22; any surprise approval or CRL would move the name and rare-disease peers.

events.title: Hurricane season tail risk (through Nov 30)
events.why_it_matters: The Atlantic season runs through Nov 30; a late-season Gulf storm would disrupt energy production and supply chains, but no specific system is currently threatening.
events.what_to_watch: NHC tropical outlooks; a named storm entering the Gulf would lift energy and insurance risk.

events.title: IFR healthcare/biotech IPO pipeline: Rezera, Vvardis, others
events.why_it_matters: Several small/mid-cap biotech and medtech IPOs priced this week; outcomes are a sentiment gauge for risk appetite in healthcare issuance.
events.what_to_watch: Aftermarket performance of Rezera and Vvardis; a broken deal would chill the biotech IPO window.

events.title: World Cup 2026 qualifiers / group stage (background, no US market impact)
events.why_it_matters: The 2026 World Cup group stage is underway, but with no matches in the US this window and limited direct market transmission, it is background context only.
events.what_to_watch: No market-moving catalyst; sports betting and media stocks may see modest flows around marquee matches.

top_risks: December Fed hike is fully priced but a 50bp move remains a live tail risk after three hot CPI prints; a hot PPI today could harden that case and trigger a broad de-risking.
Nvidia earnings (Nov 17) are the single largest binary event for the AI trade; any guidance disappointment would hit semis and broad risk appetite.
The Dec 11 government shutdown deadline is colliding with Democratic demands to restrict Iran-war funding, raising the probability of a funding lapse.
Hormuz tanker attacks and stalled Iran talks keep an oil-supply risk premium alive despite the recent price pullback; a fresh incident could push Brent back toward $100.
Anthropic's IPO pricing is a valuation test for the entire AI complex; a weak debut would pressure private AI marks and late-stage venture sentiment.
top_opportunities: The $166B IEEPA tariff refund process is a cash-flow windfall for retailers and importers, with Target and Walmart already receiving partial refunds.
China's extended tariff suspension and fresh PBoC stimulus commitments reduce near-term tail risk for trade-exposed industrials and consumer names.
South Korea's 331% YoY chip export surge confirms AI-driven demand is intact, supporting semis and equipment makers into Nvidia's print.
Retail earnings (HD, Target, Walmart) could show resilient consumer demand and margin recovery, offering a positive counterweight to macro gloom if guidance is strong.
The EU's first formal AI strategy discussion and potential Ukraine funding progress at the Nov 26-27 summit could support European equities and the euro.
summary: Markets are digesting a historic Democratic midterm sweep and a third hot CPI print that has December Fed hike odds at 100%, with a 50bp tail re-emerging. The next two weeks are dominated by Nvidia and Anthropic's IPO, US PPI and retail sales, China activity data, and fragile geopolitical talks on Ukraine and Iran. Uncertainty is elevated because a single hot PPI or weak AI guide could swing rate expectations and the AI trade.
